title: Docebo vs. Workera: AI skills platform comparison for 2027
summary: Compare Docebo and Workera on skills intelligence, AI readiness assessments, learning delivery, AI agents, pricing, and which platform fits your goals.
body_markdown:
Choosing between Docebo and Workera comes down to how you want to build your skills picture and what you want to do with it. Workera verifies skills for the employees who take its assessments. Docebo Skills Intelligence infers skills across your whole workforce and connects them to learning, internal mobility, and workforce planning. Both address skills and AI readiness, but they approach them from very different angles.


**Docebo** is an AI workforce readiness platform that connects learning, skills intelligence, knowledge, and AI agents to close the loop from skill gap to learning to verified readiness.


**Workera** describes itself as a skills intelligence and assessment platform that verifies what employees and candidates can do, including AI readiness, through its Skills Intelligence Engine and four AI agents. Pearson[announced plans to acquire](https://plc.pearson.com/en-GB/news-and-insights/news/pearson-acquires-workera-pioneer-ai-native-enterprise-assessment-and-skills) Workera in September 2026.


This guide compares them on skills intelligence, AI readiness assessment, learning delivery, AI agents, external audiences, integrations, pricing, and customer reviews so you can decide which platform fits your organization best.

## When Docebo is the better fit


Docebo is the stronger choice when you want to connect skills intelligence to learning and workforce action in one offering. It combines native enterprise learning delivery, Docebo Skills Intelligence, internal mobility, and workforce planning, so a skill signal becomes assigned, tracked, and proven development. Workera also offers development recommendations through Ambient Coaching. Docebo’s advantage is that learning delivery, skills intelligence, and workforce decisions share one platform.


**1) You need to act on skills data as well as measure it.**


Spotting a gap is the easy part; changing how people work is harder. Docebo’s[AI Readiness Gap Report](https://www.docebo.com/research/ai-readiness-gap-report-2026/) 2026 surveyed 2,000 enterprise respondents in six countries. Among learning leaders surveyed, 91% say their organizations have yet to fully redefine workflows with AI.


In Docebo, a detected gap feeds a learning path, and the platform delivers it, tracks progress, and records evidence of change. This loop runs in one system, so you aren’t stitching exports between tools. Your skills data finally has somewhere to go.


**2) You train customers, partners, or members as well as employees.**


Docebo runs separate branded environments per audience, which means you can cover customer education, partner enablement, and member programs from one system. Extended enterprise is included in the Enterprise tier (up to 10 domains) and available as an add-on.


**3) You want skills intelligence across the whole workforce.**


[Docebo Skills Intelligence](https://www.docebo.com/products/skills-intelligence/) , powered by 365Talents, infers skills from roles, experience, projects, and learning activity. SNCF reports[saving about €100M](https://365talents.com/en/) on temping and external consulting through skills intelligence (customer-reported, per 365Talents).


**4) Compliance and certification records matter.**


SCORM and xAPI content, recertification, and audit-ready reporting sit in the same platform where gaps get closed. Docebo automates certification and compliance tracking, so renewals don’t depend on spreadsheets. When an auditor asks who’s certified, you’ll have the answer.


**5) You want knowledge and AI agents in the flow of work.**


Docebo Knowledge connects the platform to 20+ sources, such as SharePoint and Confluence. Docebo Agents detect gaps, push learning, and create content, while Roleplay lets teams practice real conversations with AI feedback. The Docebo[Model Context Protocol](https://www.docebo.com/products/mcp/) (MCP) Server brings Docebo into Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and ChatGPT, so people get answers inside the tools they already use. Docebo Knowledge and Docebo Agents became available to all Learn customers in October 2026.


## When Workera may be the better fit


Workera is the stronger choice when proving specific skills is the urgent job. Here’s where it earns a spot on your shortlist.


**1) Skills verification is the first priority.**


Workera says it combines adaptive assessments, intelligent proctoring, custom benchmarks, and credentials across 100+ signature assessments. Compare assessment design, evidence standards, and coverage for your own roles.


**2) You want skills-based hiring.**


Workera lists a Hiring agent that verifies candidate capability before an offer. If screening candidates on evidence is your gap, that’s a direct match.


**3) You need an AI readiness baseline for leadership.**


Workera promotes its AI Readiness Index as “a defensible, board-ready baseline of AI capability” across functions, levels, and roles. Workera says its AI Readiness Index Bundle includes 10 signature assessments across five personas, such as Practitioner and Engineer. That suits executives who want a clear starting point before funding a program.


**4) You already have an LMS and only need measurement.**


If your LMS stays and you need a tested baseline, Workera is a legitimate shortlist choice. Docebo Skills Intelligence can also sit alongside an existing LMS if you’d rather infer skills across your whole workforce. Either way, ask how assessment results flow back into your LMS.


## Docebo vs. Workera: Detailed platform and capability breakdown


Both companies address skills, AI, and workforce capability, so a feature checklist won’t settle this. Compare how each platform detects skills, delivers learning and knowledge, produces evidence, and triggers the next action.


### Core platform architecture


Architecture decides what happens after you find a gap. Workera is built to measure skills, while Docebo measures, develops, and validates them in one loop.


**Workera:** Workera says its Skills Intelligence Engine reads what your workforce can do, then powers four agents: Hiring, Skills Assessments, AI Studio, and Ambient Coaching. Every agent works from the same measured picture.


**Docebo:** Learning, Docebo Skills Intelligence, Enterprise Knowledge, and Docebo Agents share data and a learner profile. A gap you detect flows into learning, and validated progress updates skills in the same system.


**Bottom line:** Workera is organized around measurement. Docebo is organized around the full readiness loop.


### Skills intelligence and evidence


Skills data is only as useful as its evidence. Workera leans on tested signals, while Docebo infers skills from everyday work.


**Workera:** Workera describes a verified signal built from assessments, benchmarks, credentials, and always-on measurement through Ambient Coaching. You get proficiency data grounded in what people demonstrate.


**Docebo:** Docebo Skills Intelligence infers skills from roles, experience, projects, and learning activity, with ongoing validation that keeps skills profiles accurate and current.


**Bottom line:** Neither relies on one signal type. Compare sources, coverage, validation, and refresh cadence.


### Assessment, verification, and AI readiness


Assessment is how you prove capability. Workera treats it as the core product, while Docebo treats it as one input into a readiness judgment.


**Workera:** Workera lists adaptive assessments, intelligent proctoring, custom benchmarks, credentials, and human-in-the-loop validation, which Workera positions as defensible proof. Its AI Readiness Index Bundle[launched May 27, 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/workera-releases-ai-readiness-assessments-aligned-to-evolving-industry-standards-302782787.html) , with assessments Workera says take 20-30 minutes.


**Docebo:** Assessments, certifications, roleplay feedback, and on-the-job checklists feed a configurable readiness judgment. It can trigger the next learning step, so a score turns into a plan.


**Bottom line:** Workera has the deeper assessment product. Docebo is stronger when results must drive development.


### Learning, knowledge, and coaching


Once you find gaps, you need a way to close them. Workera coaches in the flow of work, while Docebo delivers learning through a native LMS.


**Workera:** Workera describes Ambient Coaching as personalized learning in the flow of work, so development happens alongside daily tasks. Its homepage showed a waitlist as of October 2026, so confirm availability.


**Docebo:** The native LMS adds recommendations, AI course authoring, Enterprise Knowledge, and Roleplay, so you govern and report on learning in one place. Booking.com reports a[600% increase](https://www.docebo.com/customers/instructor-led-training/) in instructor-led training (ILT) offerings (customer-reported).


**Bottom line:** Choose Docebo when learning must be certified and reported. Workera fits when measurement and coaching come first.


### AI agents and orchestration


Both use AI agents, so ask what each one does. Workera ties each agent to one job, while Docebo’s agents act across learning tasks.


**Workera:** Workera offers four purpose-built agents, each tied to a defined job. Workera says AI Studio lets you build and launch custom assessments in a day.


**Docebo:** Docebo Agents[launched in October 2026](https://www.docebo.com/company/newsroom/docebo-expands-workforce-readiness-platform-with-launch-of-knowledge-and-agents/) with four pre-built agents: Authoring turns source material into courses, Tutor answers learner questions inside courses, Reinforcement runs spaced practice after a course ends, and Marketplace compares third-party content and imports courses. Admins can also build custom agents with no code, and they control which agents run and which actions need human approval. The MCP integration connects Docebo to Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and ChatGPT, so people can find content, check progress, and enroll without opening Docebo.


**Bottom line:** Depends. Compare each agent’s task, permissions, auditability, and current availability.


### Customer, partner, and external audiences


External training needs separate branding, content, and reporting. Docebo builds those audiences into its architecture, while Workera’s public focus is workforce and candidates.


**Workera:** Workera’s public positioning centers on the enterprise workforce and job candidates. If you plan to assess partners or customers, ask for a reference.


**Docebo:** One Docebo platform runs distinct environments for every audience. Your customer academy, partner certification, and onboarding share one system.


**Bottom line:** Docebo is the stronger fit when external training is a substantial use case.


### Hiring and talent decisions


Skills data shapes who you hire and who you move. Workera points it at candidates, while Docebo points it at your current talent.


**Workera:** The Hiring agent supports skills-based candidate evaluation, so you can screen on evidence before an offer.


**Docebo:** Skills Intelligence supports internal mobility, career pathing, and workforce planning. It can inform internal-versus-external hiring, but candidate assessment isn’t a primary use case.


**Bottom line:** Workera for candidate verification. Docebo for internal mobility tied to learning.


### Integrations, security, and governance


Both platforms must fit your stack and pass security review, and they’re closely matched here.


**Workera:** Workera’s May 2026 release says it integrates with 250+ human resources information system (HRIS), applicant tracking system (ATS), and learning management system (LMS) products. Workera’s website lists SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and ISO 42001.


**Docebo:** Docebo integrates with[HRIS](https://www.docebo.com/products/integrations/) , customer relationship management (CRM), and data and analytics tools, linking learning to business outcomes. Docebo’s information security management system complies with[ISO 27001 and SOC 2](https://www.docebo.com/solutions/enterprise-learning-management/) . Docebo Agents respect existing permissions and log every action, and Docebo Knowledge inherits the permissions of each connected source.


**Bottom line:** Tie. Check each vendor’s current documentation against your requirements.


### Implementation and support


Scope drives effort more than vendor choice. Workera rollouts center on assessment design, while Docebo’s center on audiences and content.


**Workera:** Plan around assessment design, population size, and how results reach your LMS.


**Docebo:** Plan around audiences, content migration, and integrations. Focused rollouts move faster than multi-audience migrations, so start narrow.


**Bottom line:** Tie. Ask both vendors who staffs the rollout, what costs extra, and how support works after go-live.


### Pricing and total cost of ownership


Headline prices rarely compare directly. Workera publishes a per-participant entry price, while Docebo quotes by tier and active users.


**Workera:** Workera’s AI Readiness Index Bundle starts at under $5 per participant, according to its May 2026 release. That makes a baseline easy to budget; other products are quoted.


**Docebo:** Pricing is[custom](https://www.docebo.com/pricing/) , based on your tier (Elevate or Enterprise) and active users. Docebo Skills Intelligence is priced separately. Extended enterprise is included in the Enterprise tier (up to 10 domains) or as an add-on, so scope external audiences early. Docebo Agents use AI credits that admins can monitor, so confirm expected credit usage in your quote.


**Bottom line:** Model three-year cost on the same population, integrations, and services.


## Questions to ask if Workera’s ownership changes


If the acquisition has closed by the time you read this, ask these questions before you sign:


- Who sets the product roadmap after closing?
- Who will hold your contract, and could terms change?
- Will support teams and service levels stay the same?
- Where will your data live, and under whose governance?
- Which integrations with the new owner’s products are planned?


## Docebo vs. Workera customer reviews


Ratings help, but volume matters as much as the score. As of October 2026, Docebo holds[4.3 out of 5](https://www.g2.com/products/docebo/reviews) on G2 from about 750 reviews. Workera holds[4.6 out of 5](https://www.g2.com/products/workera-ai/reviews) on G2 from 26 reviews.


Capterra shows[one Workera review](https://www.capterra.com/p/276716/Workera/) (4.0, from 2023). That’s a large volume gap, and public review evidence for Workera is thin.


Neither score proves technical superiority, and Docebo’s G2 reviews mostly cover its LMS. Re-check both listings on your decision date, and filter reviews by company size and use case.


Workera’s headline proof is ServiceNow. Workera[reports](https://www.workera.ai/) that in the first 60 days, ServiceNow rolled out to 28,000 employees, with 54,000 verified baselines and 10% average skill growth. We couldn’t find a standalone case study, so treat these as Workera-published figures.


Docebo’s proof spans both skills and learning. Booking.com, a company of more than 15,000 employees, uses Docebo. It reports[600% more](https://www.docebo.com/customers/instructor-led-training/) instructor-led training offerings and up to 80% less admin overhead on complex programs (customer-estimated). On the skills side, Société Générale[deployed 365Talents across 30+ countries and nearly 74,000 employees](https://365talents.com/en/resources/case_studies/client-use-case-societe-generale/) , according to 365Talents.


## Which platform is the right choice for your team?


Here’s the one question that matters: Do you need to verify skills, or to detect, close, and prove skill gaps in one connected platform? Use these diagnostics to decide.


- **Is your most urgent need skills verification, candidate screening, or an AI readiness baseline?** Workera is the stronger fit.
- **Do you need to assign, track, and certify learning once you find a gap?** Docebo is the stronger fit.
- **Must skills intelligence inform internal mobility and workforce planning?** Docebo Skills Intelligence is the stronger fit.
- **Do you train customers, partners, or members as well as employees?** Docebo is the stronger fit.
- **Do you need compliance records and audit-ready reporting inside your learning platform?** Docebo is the stronger fit.
- **Do you have an LMS you’ll keep, and only need measurement?** Workera is a strong shortlist pick; Docebo Skills Intelligence adds inferred skills.


Workera is the practical choice when your first job is verifying skills, hiring on evidence, or baselining AI readiness. Docebo is the stronger choice when you want to detect, develop, validate, and orchestrate workforce readiness in one platform, including for external audiences.


The two can also work together. Run a matched pilot on one real role, and the answer gets clear fast.


Ready to see skill gaps turn into measurable progress?[Take a product tour](https://www.docebo.com/take-a-tour/) or[book a demo](https://www.docebo.com/demo/) to learn more.


## FAQs


**What is the difference between Docebo and Workera?**


Docebo is an AI workforce readiness platform connecting learning, skills intelligence, knowledge, and agents. Workera is a skills intelligence and assessment platform for verifying capability. They start and end in different places. Workera starts by verifying what people can do, while Docebo starts with the gap and carries it through learning, practice, and proof of change.


**Is Workera an LMS, and can it replace one?**


Workera positions itself around skills intelligence, assessment, hiring, AI Studio, and coaching, and doesn’t market itself as a learning management system. If you’re weighing it as a replacement, confirm course administration, enrollment, compliance records, instructor-led training, and reporting in a live demo.


**How does Workera’s AI Readiness Index compare with Docebo’s approach to AI readiness?**


They aren’t equivalent scores: Workera’s index is a baseline across roles, while Docebo tracks readiness as skills, learning, knowledge, and evidence change over time. Ask each vendor what it measures, which roles it covers, how results are validated, and what happens next.


**How much does Workera cost compared with Docebo?**


Workera’s AI Readiness Index Bundle starts at under $5 per participant (as of October 2026), while broader Workera deployments and Docebo are quoted. Per-participant and active-user pricing count people differently, so convert both quotes to the same population before you compare.


**What are the best Workera alternatives?**


Consider Docebo for connected learning, skills intelligence, and external audiences, plus Degreed for a skills-first learning experience.[Eightfold AI](https://www.docebo.com/learning-network/blog/docebo-vs-eightfold/) and Fuel50 suit buyers focused on talent intelligence and internal mobility.


**Can Docebo and Workera be used together?**


Yes, they can be complementary, since Workera’s assessment results could inform the learning Docebo assigns. Don’t assume a native integration; confirm data flows and integration scope with both vendors’ technical teams.


**What should buyers ask during a Docebo or Workera demo?**


Give both vendors the same real role and ask them to show, live, how a skill signal becomes an action and then evidence. Then ask which features are generally available today and which are still on the roadmap.
